recipes.name: Baked Ham and Cheese Sliders
ingredients_raw: 1 pound thinly sliced cooked deli ham

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix butter, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, poppy seeds, and dried onion in a bowl.

Separate the tops from the bottoms of the rolls; arrange the bottom pieces in a layer in the prepared baking dish. Layer about 1/2 of the ham onto the rolls; add a layer of Swiss cheese and top with remaining ham slices.
Place the tops of the rolls onto the sandwiches. Pour mustard mixture evenly over the rolls
Bake in the preheated oven until the rolls are lightly browned and the cheese has melted, about 20 minutes. Slice into individual rolls through the ham and cheese layers to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Ham and Cheese Sliders
raw_recipe.description: These baked ham and cheese sliders layer deli ham and Swiss cheese on soft rolls with a buttery Dijon-poppy seed topping for an easy party appetizer.

video.description:
There's never a bad time to eat irresistibly decadent ham and cheese sliders. The party-friendly sandwiches in this video boast buttery rolls that surround savory deli meat, melted Swiss cheese, and sharp, spicy Dijon mustard. 
Whether you're feeding a large crowd or a family of four, these perfectly delicious oven-baked sliders are a surefire way to make it a celebratory occasion.

review.reviewBody: I made these for the first time last night and the family loved them. I used butter flavored hawaiian rolls and doubled the dijon mustard. I also left out the poppy seeds and used a mixture of minced garlic and onion powder (1 tbsp total). I made 12 with swiss cheese and 12 with muenster cheese. Don't be afraid to pour the entire mixture over the rolls. I was worried it was way too much at first and left some in the bowl. I was wrong! The topping cooks into the rolls perfectly. This recipe is definitely a keeper. Thanks Lisa!

I've made these before but grabbed this recipe quickly to make for a party. After I took them out of the oven I realized I like them better when they're covered with foil and baked 10 minutes, then remove the foil. These were okay, but not as good as when they're covered first.

Growing up we had a variation of this we called "poker sandwiches" because Mom made them when Dad's friends came over to play poker. We used yellow mustard, onions, butter and poppy seeds with ham and swiss cheese and made the sandwiches individually with the mustard, onion, butter mixture on the inside of the sandwich. We wrapped them individually in foil, froze them, and popped them in the oven for poker night. Our version was always a hit and you can make a ton and keep them on hand for after-school snacks.

This is my go-to sandwich recipe when there are family/friend gatherings. So easy, so delicious. I do something different with the butter though. Instead of melting it I just let it get soft and mix all the ingredients into the butter (mustard, worcestershire, poppy seeds and onions)then spread the tops of the rolls (the inside part) before putting the sandwiches back together before baking. Great recipe! Thanks for sharing!

I found the original recipe online from King's Hawaiian rolls, and there is a critical step: "Drizzle butter mixture over ham and cheese, but save some to brush the top of your rolls with." Next time, I will definitely be doing that!! I thought it was odd that you would pour all of the mixture on top! The mixture runs off into the bottom of the dish, saturating only the bottom buns and making the bun tops hard. It felt like the mixture should be poured BEFORE adding the tops, and I was right! Also, next time I will add caramelized onions as a layer, rather than adding in minced onion or onion powder. And I will also cover the dish with foil until the last 5 minutes. Otherwise,, they dry out and the tops get too hard.

If I could give these babies a 10 I would. I made them for our annual superbowl party and they were a hit! Three people asked for the recipe. I followed other reviewers advice and used the smaller King Hawaiian Rolls and left them in a block while removing the top from the bottom. I added a little mayo, then the ham, then cheese. Put the top back on a cut each sandwich seperately and placed on cookie sheet about 1/2 inch apart. Baked for 10 minutes with foil on and 10 minutes uncovered. They were amazing! These will now be a staple at all of our parties!
Perfect! I did spread some Chive Cream Cheese on the rolls before adding the other ingredients. I also used Roast Beef and Horseradish Cheddar on half of the sandwiches.

Per recommendations, instead of poppy seeds, we used "everything" bagel seasoning and provolone and mozzarella instead of Swiss, and they came out great. My 16 year old made these without any help, and our guests loved them and came back for seconds and thirds during the Super Bowl. Easy clean-up! Definitely a keeper.

I made it with Costco’s dinner rolls. I think they come in a 48 pack. I used shaved Italian rosemary ham and havarti cheese. I combined Johnny’s garlic spread dry seasoning from Costco with the melted unsalted butter and pored it all on top. I thought it was going to be too greasy but it surprisingly wasn’t. I put it on convection bake at 350 for 13 minutes covered then 8 minutes uncoverered. Served with Caesar salad. This was absolutely delicious with no leftovers.

Great recipe! Only changes I made were I covered them the entire bake time, and sliced them before I drizzled and cooked them. (It made them much easier to handle than the first time I made a similar recipe.) Excellent party food!

I love these, and I always forget to make them. It’s just like deviation this time where they did half of them with white cheddar and ham and the other half with ham and Swiss. Also spread a thin layer of blackberry jam on the bread before I compile them. Also, put a tablespoon of brown sugar in the butter. Mixture before putting it on top. Delicious. Sidenote. These burn pretty quickly at the bottom if not watching what you’re doing. I put a piece of parchment paper to line my pan before I put the sandwiches in the dish.

The only problem I had was that the rolls burned on the bottom of the baking dish and it was so hard to cut them. I did my best but one person told me they were burned on the bottom. I felt bad but I didn't answer. Everyone ate them jus the same including her.

I made these and they were wonderful. My picky husband loved them. My tweaks for next time: go easy on the bottom layer of sauce or they get soggy, add more syrup when making the sauce, overall use less salt.
Easy, simple, and delicious.
My Collage RA loves them
My family love these!
A standout at a pot luck party, these sliders are great with Havarti cheese too.

I recently made a bunch of food for my colleagues and this recipe got devoured most of all. I generally followed the recipe but made it a bit larger so I guessed on the proportions and it still came out perfectly. I will be making this recipe on repeat for work.
Everyone loved it. I did use Everything Bagel instead of poppy seeds - only because I didn’t have any. Wonderful recipe. I’ve made it several times and always a hit!
These are amazing, we make them with hawaiian rolls and they are just wonderful, but very rich, a guilty pleasure so we don't make too often. Highly recommend. Thank you LisaT!
